transcript:
Header: 2026-05-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lisa Gomez (Redwood CSM); Ravi Menon (Arkadia CTO), Sofia Alvarez (ML Eng), Ben Chu (Infra), Dana Park (PM)

[00:00] Maya: ok uh good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining the weekly pulse. quick check — everyone still seeing the same dashboard?
[00:06] Ravi: Yep, looks good. we had the load generator on since last night.
[00:10] Arjun: Awesome. i'll pull up the tokens per dollar sheet — maya i think you updated it?
[00:14] Maya: yes, pushed a new tab with the tokens per dollar and tokens per second calc. there's a column for KV cache hit rate assumptions.
[00:21] Ben: quick Q, that KV cash — you mean KV cache right? the spreadsheet shows a 42% hit rate but in our run it's closer to 28.
[00:30] Sofia: yeah i'm seeing lower than expected prefix cache hits, probably because our prompts vary a lot.
[00:36] Arjun: okay so two things: first, our measurement uses windowed traffic from the assistant paths which have a higher prefix reuse. your workload has broader prompt entropy so that reduces cache effectiveness, second, batching needs to be sized differently.
[00:50] Dana: can you explain the tokens/sec/$ metric again, the column C?
[00:54] Maya: sure — tokens per second per dollar is basically throughput divided by the per-hour cost normalized to tokens. so higher is better. we compute tokens/sec/$ over a 1hr window for the run.
[01:06] Speaker 1: we also include a tail-latency penalty, so if >95th percentile latency crosses your SLO the effective tokens/sec/$ drops in the model.
[01:16] Ravi: That tail is our main worry — we need sub-200ms p95 for interactive features.
[01:21] Arjun: right, and that's where batching tradeoffs show up. more aggressive batching gives better tokens/sec/$ but can push p95 higher. we saw in yesterday's run throughput increase 1.8x when moving from batch size 1 to 8 but p95 moved from 110ms to 280ms.
[01:35] Sofia: ouch. we can't accept that 280. in practice some flows can tolerate 300ms but the chat widget is immediate.
[01:42] Maya: so we tried adaptive batching — smaller batches for low-latency routes and larger for background bulk. the spreadsheet has a sample routing policy.
[01:49] Ben: what's the dedicated pool cost vs hosted? the delta is pretty big if we reserve GPUs.
[01:53] Maya: Dedicated has a higher fixed monthly but lower variable per-token cost and you get isolation. for your current run, the break-even was around 6M tokens/day given your expected traffic pattern.
[02:04] Dana: we won't hit 6M tokens/day for a few months; right now it's more like 700k/day.
[02:09] Arjun: in that case, short term hosted with strict routing rules + aggressive prefix caching is cheaper. but if you plan to scale mid-year, dedicated becomes attractive.
[02:17] Ravi: what about quantization, like 4-bit? does that invalidate our accuracy?
[02:22] Arjun: we tested 4-bit quant with the model family you're using — small degradation on long-form and hallucination cases, but within your eval thresholds per the pre-release evals. we can turn on mixed precision to keep the quality bar.
[02:33] Sofia: i noticed the runtime logs show more cache evictions than expected at high concurrency — maybe the KV cache slot size is too small?
[02:39] Arjun: correct — by default the cache window was tuned for medium payloads. increasing slots and extending TTL improved hit rate in our synthetic test. there's a memory/latency tradeoff, though — higher slots increase memory usage on the worker but don't add latency.
[02:52] Ben: memory is okay, but we also saw occasional GC pauses on the infra side during the stress run — could be our docker settings.
[02:58] Speaker 2: (muffled) yep we had container oom events earlier but upgraded nodes.
[03:04] Maya: let's go into the numbers — Arjun, can you read the tokens/sec/$ from the last run?
[03:08] Arjun: sure, so baseline run (no caching, batch 1) tokens/sec/$ ~= 12.3. with current caching (observed 28% hit) and batch 4 we measured tokens/sec/$ ~= 18.6. with tuned cache to 42% estimated and batch 8 idealized we model tokens/sec/$ ~= 31.4, but that idealized case pushes p95 above 250ms.
[03:29] Dana: how confident are you in that modeled 42%? that's quite a jump.
[03:33] Arjun: it's based on prompt normalization and prefix consolidation we can run; if Sofia can re-run the alignment job to canonicalize prompts we usually gain 10-15% hit rate. plus some client-side memoization helps.
[03:44] Sofia: we can do that, but it will require a small change to the prompt builder. might be 1 sprint.
[03:49] Ravi: so action plan here is to push for caching improvements + adaptive batching. any blockers?
[03:53] Maya: security was a tentative blocker — Ben flagged VPC/KMS integration for the dedicated option. we need Redwood's security doc and sample network diagram.
[04:01] Ben: yeah we need SSO/SAML mappings and audit log retention details.
[04:05] Lisa: we have the SOC2 report and sample audit log pipeline, we'll share. Maya will attach docs.
[04:11] Dana: another question — what about routing fallback? if the dedicated pool saturates, do we fail open to hosted?
[04:16] Arjun: yes we can configure smart routing policies — failover to compatible hosted variants, we can also clamp token per request to limit cost. there's also warm standby to reduce cold start latency.
[04:26] Ravi: what's the expected cost on failover? if we fall back to hosted, do we risk double billing?
[04:31] Maya: no double billing; you'll pay per the endpoint you hit. the routing policy logs show per-request cost attribution.
[04:37] Ben: any specific blockers on our side to run the 24hr stress run? we need instructions.
[04:42] Maya: Arjun will hand over the load generator config and a runbook.
[04:46] Arjun: yes, i'll attach the k6 script and sample metrics queries. also we'll add a recommended nginx front with cache hints for static assistant assets — that improved effective tokens/sec/$ in our benchmark.
[04:57] Sofia: one more thing — we saw a weird tokenization variance between your tokenizer and ours, outputs had extra spaces and token counts differed by ~3% which impacts cost projections.
[05:07] Arjun: can you paste sample tokenized output? sometimes model tokenizers differ if you chop whitespace or feed unicode normals.
[05:13] Sofia: i'll add examples in the ticket after the call.
[05:17] Maya: ok recap — next steps: maya share cost model, arjun share batching + cache configs + load scripts, ben provision pool, sofia run prompt canonicalization and tokenization check. we'll reconvene next Thursday same time to review the 24hr run.
[05:30] Ravi: sounds good. question — any quick wins to reduce cost now?
[05:33] Arjun: yes: enable prefix cache with current TTL increase, add client memoization on repeat prompts, and route bulk jobs to batch-optimized endpoint. those three give quick 15-25% saving.
[05:43] Dana: can you estimate the savings in $ terms for our typical 700k/day?
[05:47] Maya: rough math — at 700k/day current tokens/sec/$ gives X cost of around $2.8k/month. with the quick wins we project $2.1k-2.4k. once you hit 6M/day the dedicated break-even flips.
[05:58] Ben: please put that dollar table in the spreadsheet, it's easier for finance.
[06:02] Maya: will do.
[06:04] Speaker 3: (cut) sorry, late to join.
[06:06] Maya: no problem. last note — security review scheduling, Lisa will send the SSO/KMS checklist and we'll book a slot with your security team.
[06:13] Lisa: i'll send an invite for the week of 5/22.
[06:16] Ravi: perfect. thanks everyone.
[06:18] Maya: thanks, we will follow up with the attachments.

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels (Speaker 1/2/3), minor recognition errors e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache" and tokenization counts approximate.

End of transcript.
